title: Onboarding-KB value: 14% floor → 57% ceiling = the value of code-reading
summary:
Trustworthy measurement of onboarding-KB competence value, cold-vs-KB on non-recoverable probes (rationale/findings/conventions) + controls, applied-correctness LLM judge. FLOOR (cold has repo access): kb_earned_project=14% (1/7) — cold reads the source and reconstructs most facts. CEILING (both arms denied repo access via empty cwd + --tools \"\" + no-access preamble, verified no fabrication): kb_earned_project=57% (4/7), cold_rate_project dropped 86%→29%, controls stayed 100%, guard trustworthy=true. The 14%→57% bracket IS the value of code-reading: ~3/7 project facts are reconstructible from the repo, so KB's standalone value concentrates where reading code is unavailable/expensive (large codebases, latency, no-access). Product thesis: onboarding-KB pays for (a) non-recoverable analytical conclusions/rationale always, (b) all project knowledge when reading is costly. VERDICT: GO on the learning loop /11 — real, judge-verified competence. One both-FAIL (escalation-set) was a retrieval-recall gap (the note existed but search didn't surface it), so the ceiling could exceed 57% with better retrieval — the loop should improve retrieval, not just add notes.</summary>
